short: A grueling jungle campaign where Australian forces successfully halted the Japanese overland advance towards Port Moresby.
full:
From 21 July to 16 November 1942, Australian and Japanese forces fought a brutal campaign along the Kokoda Track, a treacherous, muddy trail winding through the rugged Owen Stanley Range in Papua. Following their failure to take Port Moresby by sea at the Battle of the Coral Sea, the Japanese attempted an overland advance to capture the strategic port and threaten the Australian mainland.

Initially heavily outnumbered, young and inexperienced Australian militia forces fought a desperate fighting withdrawal through dense jungle, steep mountains, and tropical disease. Reinforced by seasoned veterans returning from the Middle East, the Australians eventually halted the Japanese advance just thirty miles from Port Moresby. Suffering from starvation and severed supply lines, the Japanese were forced into a disastrous retreat, marking their first land defeat of the war.
